issues.legal_issue: A public charity is a religious charity when it has a real connection with a Hindu festival or observance of a religious character, even if festival administrators do not control it and it is not an integral part of the festival.
material_facts: A fund established with contributions, subscriptions, and donations was used to feed Brahmin pilgrims attending a shrine during its Rathotsavam festival.
The feeding took place outside the temple, and the temple authorities had no control or supervision over the charity.
The charity was found to be public, and its primary purpose was to feed pilgrims attending the festival.
Some surplus income was used for other religious observances.
issues.conclusion: The fund was a religious charity because its public feeding charity had a real connection with the religious festival. The appeal was allowed and the trial court’s order was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(13) of the Madras Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1951 defines a religious charity as a public charity associated with a Hindu festival or observance of a religious character, whether or not connected with a math or temple. In context, “associated” means connected with or in relation to; it requires a real, not imaginary, connection, but does not require control by those administering the festival or that the charity be an integral part of it. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.religious_charity_classification_proceed: The proceeding asks whether a charity falls within the legal category of a religious charity.
predicates.public_charity: The charity is established or administered for a public charitable purpose.
predicates.serves_people_attending_religious_festiv: The charity provides its service to people attending a festival of a religious character.

issues.definition: When a proceeding classifies a public charity and the charity serves people attending a religious festival, the charity is a religious charity.
